To use Truss in a non-local environment you must both enable it and authorize the viewers. See Authorization.

It exits `0` when clean, `1` when a finding is at or above the `--fail-on` level (default `error`), and `2` on a bad option or a snapshot error, so a migration that introduces a problem can fail the build. Presets (`recommended`, `strict`, `none`), per-rule severity and enable / disable, ignore patterns, and the fail level are all configurable under `truss.doctor`. See the configuration reference.
Every finding carries a stable code (e.g. `TRUSS-IDX-001`) shown in both the command and the panel; the schema doctor guide lists all the rule codes and what each checks.

If your project uses Laravel Boost, Truss ships guidelines and a skill that Boost finds on its own, so an agent set up through Boost knows Truss is installed and reaches for your real schema. There is no MCP server to wire up by hand for this path.
|**MCP server**|The richest surface: five tools and a resource, queried on demand, always current|`composer require laravel/mcp`, then point your client at `php artisan mcp:start truss`|
|**Laravel Boost**|The lowest friction if you already use Boost, across every agent Boost configures|`php artisan boost:install`, tick Truss|
|**`truss:export`**|CI, scripts, and any CLI-capable agent; no optional dependency at all|None, it ships with Truss|

The commands take the same options as their artisan counterparts and run the same code, so the text exports and the doctor report are byte-identical to what artisan prints. The exit codes match too: `0` clean, `1` doctor findings at the fail level or export drift with `--check`, and `2` for anything else, including a bad connection string, an unreachable host, an unknown option, or a PHP older than 8.2. An unreachable database can never be read as a schema with problems. The full reference is on the docs site.
Prefer to design it visually? The **theme builder** lets you dial in colours and fonts against a live dashboard preview and copy the config block straight into `config/truss.php`.

Truss exposes structure only and never queries row data. Access is protected by the fixed `viewTruss` gate. The standalone binary has no gate: there is no route to protect, and whoever runs it already holds the database credentials. It reads structure only, like the package, and its error messages never contain the connection string. If you discover a security issue, please email hello@albertoarena.it rather than opening a public issue.

Using Filament? albertoarena/filament-truss puts this diagram inside your admin, as a page rather than a frame around the dashboard. It is built from the panel's own components and takes the panel's own theme, so a custom panel needs no configuration. Access follows Truss, not the panel: `truss.enabled` first, then the `viewTruss` gate outside `local`, so being let into the admin is not on its own permission to read the structure. The guide is at trussphp.com/filament.

sqlite> CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE llvm_base_of USING clangql (base_of, clangd-index.llvm.org:5900);
sqlite> CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE llvm_overridden_by USING clangql (overridden_by, clangd-index.llvm.org:5900);
sqlite> CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE llvm_refs USING clangql (refs, clangd-index.llvm.org:5900);
sqlite> SELECT Name, Scope, DefPath FROM llvm_symbols WHERE Name = "Foo"

sqlite> SELECT subclass.Name, subclass.Scope, subclass.DefPath FROM llvm_symbols AS superclass INNER JOIN llvm_base_of AS rel ON rel.Subject = superclass.Id INNER JOIN llvm_symbols AS subclass ON subclass.Id = rel.Object WHERE superclass.Name = "MCAsmInfo";
sqlite> SELECT decl.Name FROM llvm_symbols AS decl INNER JOIN llvm_refs AS ref ON ref.SymbolId = decl.Id WHERE decl.Scope = "std::" AND ref.Declaration = 1;
